transcript:
Header: 2026-06-30 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~58 minutes | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Ethan Rivera (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (Redwood Solutions Eng), Samantha Lee (HealthForge CTO), Jon Park (HealthForge DevOps), Lina Gomez (HealthForge SecOps), Marcus Dyer (HealthForge Platform)

Summary: quick sync on current state of the Redwood Private VPC pilot. Focus on network connectivity, routing glitches we saw last week, plan for the upcoming runtime upgrade, and an initial review of latency/throughput numbers from the mini-benchmark run.

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we got the usuals from our side, maya and oliver in the room, thanks for making time
[00:07] Samantha: yep thanks, we've got jon, lina and marcus on our end
[00:12] Maya: quick agenda, recap what changed since last week, network tests, upgrade window, perf numbers, and then security open questions
[00:20] Jon: quick note, we pushed the updated peering yesterday, there was a small NX thing where one route was missing, we've added it but want the SE to validate
[00:30] Maya: ok we validated basic connectivity, the missing route was to the redwood-control plane ip range, looks fixed now but the MTU mismatch is still causing fragmentation at high throughput
[00:42] Marcus: yeah at about 3Gbps we saw packet drops, thought we had 9k jumbo enabled but turns out some of our subnets had 1500 enforced by the cloud provider
[00:55] Ethan: right that explains the tail latency spikes in the logs you sent, fragmentation leads to retries and that blows up token latency
[01:05] Samantha: can you explain a bit more about token latency vs tail latency? sometimes our PMs confuse those
[01:12] Oliver: sure, token latency is per-token generation latency; tail latency is the high-percentile spikes often caused by network retries, cold kv cache, or oversized batches
[01:26] Lina: on the security side i'm still waiting on KMS integration details, like whether keys live in our KMS or Redwood's, and how key rotation looks
[01:34] Ethan: good point, quick summary: for Private we support customer-managed KMS - keys stay in your KMS and we use envelope encryption, rotation works via your normal rotation hooks. i'll follow up with the integration doc after the call
[01:46] Lina: thanks, also need clarity on audit logs retention, we have a 7 year requirement for some flows
[01:53] Maya: we capture request-level audit logs and can push them to your S3 endpoint or syslog; retention can be configured on your side. we'll put together a retention architecture note for you
[02:05] Jon: back to networking, can you re-run the KV cache warmup with MTU set to 1500 so we can reproduce the drop? previous test used 9000 which masked the issue
[02:15] Maya: yes we'll run two sets: 1500 and 9000, and include pcap samples. expected timeframe 48 hours
[02:23] Samantha: also curious about the upcoming runtime/agent upgrade, what's the plan and is there a rollback?
[02:29] Oliver: plan is to deploy v1.9.3 runtime that has improved attention kernel selection and a fix for the memory leak we hit in the earlier build. rollout is staged: dev-hosted -> canary in your pilot cluster -> full pilot. there's an automated rollback on any OOM or high-error-rate trigger
[02:45] Marcus: how long is the window? our change freeze is 10pm PST so ideally we want upgrades during the maintenance window at 1am
[02:51] Ethan: we can do that. Proposed maintenance window: 01:00-02:30 local (PST) on 2026-07-07. We'll coordinate with your on-call
[03:01] Samantha: any expected latency impact during the upgrade?
[03:05] Maya: minimal for most requests because we phase canary and drain connections. You might see small increases in tail latency briefly during cutover; we'll push traffic to fallback model variant if that happens
[03:17] Jon: speaking of fallback, can you remind us how the routing policy works? our app needs deterministic failover to the hosted tier if local capacity is exhausted
[03:26] Oliver: yes, smart routing policy can failover by model family and by region. For Private you can set a policy: strict (no failover), best-effort (attempt local then hosted) or always-fallback. For this pilot we recommended best-effort and a hard cap on request concurrency
[03:43] Lina: we prefer strict for sensitive data flows, but for non-PHI we could do best-effort. how do you classify flows?
[03:51] Ethan: you can tag routes - route-level metadata marks a request as sensitive. Those tagged can be routed strict to Private and blocked from hosted fallback
[04:00] Samantha: ok that helps. can we see the tagging api example?
[04:04] Ethan: yes i'll send the snippet and the console screenshot after
[04:09] Jon: network perf - any preliminary numbers from the mini-benchmark you ran against our cluster?
[04:15] Maya: initial run (9000 MTU) showed sustained token throughput of ~260k tokens/min across the pool and median per-token latency of 12ms, p95 at 90ms. With MTU=1500 the throughput dropped to ~180k tokens/min and p95 went to 140ms due to fragmentation and extra retries
[04:33] Marcus: that's pretty significant, any quick tuning we can try?
[04:36] Maya: yes, we'll try two knobs: reduce batch size by 15% and enable more aggressive prefix caching for common prompts. that should reduce network pressure and lower tail latency
[04:48] Samantha: how does prefix caching interact with KV cache warmup? I thought those were the same
[04:54] Oliver: related but different: KV cache is low-level transformer cache per-session; prefix caching stores pre-computed embeddings or model prefixes for common prompts. Warmup primes the KV cache so first requests aren't cold
[05:08] Jon: are there any firewall rules for outbound connections from our VPC to Redwood you need us to allow beyond 443? we had a security reviewer ask if there are health check ports
[05:15] Maya: outbound 443 is the primary. For control-plane health checks we also use 8443 and occasionally ephemeral high ports for websocket keepalive. We'll send an exact list.
[05:25] Lina: does Redwood use static IPs for control plane? we need to whitelist IPs not ranges for our corporate firewall
[05:30] Ethan: we provide static egress IPs for Dedicated but for Private we can offer an IP-allowlist for the control plane; it's a managed pool and we'll provide the set ahead of the upgrade. I'll surface the doc
[05:42] Samantha: ok next on the perf sheet - you mentioned a memory leak fix; did that materially change our memory usage profiles?
[05:48] Oliver: in our internal testing v1.9.3 reduces per-model host mem growth by ~20% under sustained load. For your pilot we saw more stable resident set size in the canary run last night
[05:58] Marcus: great, any guidance on swap/no-swap settings? cloud provider recommends swap off for GPUs
[06:03] Maya: we recommend not using swap for GPU hosts; it can block the driver. We'll add that to the ops checklist
[06:10] Jon: action item: i'll rerun BGP route advertisements after we fix MTU and let you know results
[06:16] Ethan: perfect. On the security doc question, lina, i'll attach an FAQ about KMS envelope encryption and key custody after the call
[06:25] Lina: please include rotation cadence examples; our audit needs that to verify controls
[06:30] Maya: another quick point - if you want deterministic failover we can pin model weights to a variant in the hosted catalog that matches quantization level. that way you don't get cross-variant behavior during fallback
[06:42] Samantha: interesting, what's the difference in quality if we pin to a quantized variant?
[06:46] Oliver: in our evals the 4-bit quantized variant shows minor drop in long-tail instruction following but median quality for chat tasks is comparable. We'll provide eval results for your prompt set so you can compare
[07:00] Samantha: please do that. also timelines - what's the decision point for pilot -> dedicated?
[07:06] Ethan: typically after stability and performance criteria are met for two consecutive weeks and security signoff, we propose moving to reserved capacity. We'll draft a proposal once your perf tests complete
[07:16] Jon: question on pricing - do you charge for audit log egress?
[07:20] Ethan: logs pushed to your S3 are included in the Private package up to a retention threshold; large archival egress may incur extra fees, we'll clarify in the pricing note
[07:30] Lina: last security nit, do you support SAML SSO for console?
[07:33] Maya: yes, SAML and SCIM user provisioning - we'll share the SSO setup guide
[07:38] Ethan: ok recap and next steps: SE will run MTU=1500 KV warmup and share pcap and csv by 2026-07-02; SE to try reduced batch size + prefix caching and post results; AE will send pricing and static-ip options by 2026-07-06; Security doc for KMS/audit retention to Lina by 2026-07-03; schedule maintenance window proposed for 2026-07-07 01:00-02:30 PST for runtime upgrade.
[07:59] Samantha: thanks, that works for us
[08:02] Ethan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread and i'll attach the network checklist and SSO doc
[08:10] Meeting ended
